> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


The intent (gate PR descriptions so merge commits carry a parseable Launchpad bug reference) is sound, and the keyword list correctly mirrors lp-bug-update.yaml. However, the validation regex is inverted relative to this PR's stated goal: it accepts the legacy `LP: <id>` form and rejects the `LP: #<id>` form the commit says it is standardizing on — which is also the only `LP:` form Launchpad actually parses (per the linked comment-syntax doc, the multi-bug pattern is `LP: #<number>[, #<number>]...`; `LP: 123` without `#` does not link). As written, PRs using the documented standard will fail CI, while PRs using the old form will pass and still be invisible to Launchpad's own parsing. The regex (and the matching extractor in lp-bug-update.yaml) should accept an optional `#`, and the error message should be updated to match.

.github/workflows/ci.yaml.172: Bug: `LP:\s*\K[0-9]+` requires a digit immediately after `LP:` + whitespace, so it rejects `LP: #2066936` — the format this PR says it is standardizing on, and the only `LP:` form Launchpad's comment parser actually links (`LP: #<n>` per the linked docs). Meanwhile it accepts the legacy `LP: 2066936`, which Launchpad does not parse. Suggest `LP:\s*#?\s*\K[0-9]+` here and in the extractor in lp-bug-update.yaml, otherwise the gate enforces a format that disagrees with both the stated standard and Launchpad.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.174: Error message contradicts the PR's stated standard: it tells authors to use `LP:<number>` while the commit message and Launchpad docs specify `LP: #<number>`. Update together with the regex so the guidance matches what is accepted.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.171: Limitation worth noting: the closing keyword and the `LP:` reference must be on the same line (`.` does not match newlines in this PCRE), so a body like `Fixes\nLP: #123` silently skips the check. The same constraint exists in lp-bug-update.yaml, so behavior is consistent, but multi-line references will evade both the gate and the bug-status update.
